title: United wins Spa as G-Drive crashes from the lead
dek: Phil Hanson and Filipe Albuquerque won the 4 Hours of Spa in the pole-sitting United Oreca #22 after Mikkel Jensen crashed the leading G-Drive Aurus at Pouhon in the final hour.

chapters.title: Back-to-back weekends at Spa
text: The 4 Hours of Spa-Francorchamps on 9 August 2020 was the second round of a European Le Mans Series season already pushed into mid-summer by the pandemic, and it opened a double bill at the Belgian circuit, with the FIA World Endurance Championship arriving a week later. The calendar was still shifting: days before the race the series replaced the planned 4 Hours of Barcelona on 29 August with a second four-hour race at Le Castellet, because rising COVID-19 numbers in Catalonia would have meant quarantines for teams only weeks before the Le Mans 24 Hours. A new UK quarantine rule for travellers from Belgium, announced on the Thursday evening, also rattled the British contingent, although most paddock staff were expected to receive exemption letters; the Red River Sport Ferrari #62 withdrew regardless.

The entry was unusual. JOTA made its first ELMS appearance under its own name since 2015, running a guest Oreca #38 for Anthony Davidson, Roberto Gonzalez and Jake Dennis. Four FIA WEC GTE cars joined the class, making a 12-car field, the biggest since Estoril in 2014. G-Drive Racing ran its Aurus #26 with only Roman Rusinov and Mikkel Jensen because its usual stand-ins were at the Berlin E-Prix. Richard Mille Racing gave W Series runner-up Beitske Visser her prototype debut alongside Tatiana Calderon and Andre Negrao, with Katherine Legge still recovering from her pre-season testing crash. Earlier in the week Thomas Flohr had crashed the AF Corse Ferrari #54 at the Esses, damage beyond repair at the circuit, and a replacement car was built up for the weekend.

chapters.title: United locks out the front row
text: United Autosports took the first two places on the grid in the 12-minute session. Filipe Albuquerque put the #22 Oreca on pole with 2:03.298, his fourth ELMS pole in a row, after Mikkel Jensen had led the early running for G-Drive. With seven minutes left Albuquerque set a 2:03.471 benchmark, then United called both cars in for fresh tyres and improved: Job van Uitert took the #32 car to second on 2:03.817, four thousandths ahead of Jensen's Aurus #26, and Albuquerque found nearly two more tenths.

Konstantin Tereshchenko was fourth for Duqueine Team and Anthony Davidson climbed from seventh to fifth in the JOTA Oreca #38, the best of the Goodyear-shod cars, as Michelin runners filled the first two rows. Ben Hanley, Jon Lancaster and Richard Bradley followed in sixth to eighth for DragonSpeed, Algarve Pro Racing and IDEC Sport. United also claimed LMP3 pole through Wayne Boyd, 0.885 seconds clear of the field.

chapters.title: Heat, a Safety Car and a lead change
text: The race started in temperatures well into the 30s, with track temperature approaching 50 degrees at times. Davidson grabbed third for JOTA at the start on the grass down the Kemmel Straight, getting past Jensen, while Hanson led from pole. The first Safety Car came when Martin Hippe put the Inter Europol LMP3 Ligier #13 into the barrier at Speakers Corner while avoiding a spinning car. Shortly before the end of the hour another incident followed, as Will Owen's United Oreca #32 tapped the Iron Lynx Ferrari #60, which went hard into the wall; Owen served a stop-and-go penalty. At the first Safety Car restart Jensen got past Hanson on the Kemmel Straight and took the lead.

chapters.title: Jensen and Albuquerque trade the lead
text: The Aurus and the United Oreca spent the middle of the race swapping places. After a round of pit stops in the third hour the lead changed hands twice. Albuquerque took it on a Full Course Yellow restart after Jensen got caught behind traffic, but Jensen went back past him at Les Combes. The sister United car, meanwhile, had been put out of sequence by Owen's penalty and drifted off the podium pace. Elsewhere the pit lane produced its own drama, as the Cool Racing Oreca #37 struck a G-Drive crew member at some point during the race; the man was taken to hospital as a precaution.

chapters.title: Rain at Pouhon
text: As the final hour began, significant rain arrived briefly. Jensen's lead was short-lived: he lost the Aurus in the greasy conditions at Pouhon and slid into the barrier, ending a race in which he had passed the #22 twice. The car completed 76 laps and was not classified. Hanson, who had been pushed hard by the Aurus for most of the afternoon, put his head down and was left to cruise towards the flag. Behind him the order was still unsettled, and a late Full Course Yellow for debris brought the field together again.

chapters.title: A puncture on the final lap
text: Hanson and Albuquerque took the flag about a minute clear. The fight for second was far closer. Duqueine Team had looked set for the runner-up spot, but chose not to pit the #30 for a required splash under the late Full Course Yellow and fell to fourth when it stopped under green. At the start of the last lap Thomas Laurent in the Graff Oreca #39 and Will Stevens in the Panis Racing #31 led Tristan Gommendy by half a second across the three of them. Gommendy drew alongside Stevens out of La Source and took third, but a right rear puncture at Blanchimont sent him into a spin and he dropped back to fourth. Graff took second and Panis third, the best of the Goodyear-shod finishers.

chapters.title: Sanctions, fines and a quick turnaround
text: It was a first win of the season for the United pair and, on an afternoon crowded with penalties, a calm drive for a crew that Jensen had passed twice. The margin of about a minute disguised how close the lead battle had been until the G-Drive mistake. Richard Mille Racing scored a steady points finish in sixth, and IDEC Sport recovered from the broken wiring loom that wrecked its opener.

The stewards then turned to the pit lane. The Cool Racing Oreca #37 that hit the G-Drive mechanic was completely exonerated, but the incident was held against G-Drive Racing itself. The team was sanctioned both for not ensuring the safety of the pit stop and for moving the injured crew member in a way that could have harmed him. It was ordered to accomplish some work of public interest and to take part in extraction exercises at the next three ELMS races, with the team manager and car controller both required to attend. The crew member was back at the circuit later that evening.

There was a smaller sanction for DKR Engineering, fined 250 euros after Jean Glorieux took the chequered flag twice at the end of the race. The wider backdrop stayed uncertain: the Barcelona round was gone, and the Le Mans 24 Hours, postponed to 19-20 September, was confirmed to run behind closed doors the day after the race.

The turnaround was immediate. Within about 90 minutes of the flag, teams were already rearranging their garages for the WEC round the following weekend, with AF Corse rolling out its GTE Pro Ferraris, Proton reorganising and JOTA preparing to expand from one car to two. For the European Le Mans Series the next stop was Le Castellet on 29 August, now the third round of the season.

facts.v: Filipe Albuquerque took pole with 2:03.298 in the #22 Oreca, his fourth consecutive ELMS pole, and United locked out the front row.
Mikkel Jensen lost the Aurus in greasy conditions at Pouhon in the final hour, handing United the win.
Tristan Gommendy took third from Stevens on the last lap, then a right rear puncture dropped the Duqueine to fourth.
Stewards ordered G-Drive to do public-interest work and take part in extraction exercises at the next three ELMS races after the pit-lane incident.
The 4 Hours of Barcelona on 29 August was swapped for a second four-hour race at Le Castellet.
